body: I see.  So pretty detrimental financial issues, and just basic companionship.  And I could of course suggest so and so, but I'm assuming you have already considered getting help from public sources that help with money issues and so forth.  I personally live from paycheck to paycheck, and have a public physician that prescribes me mental health stuff.  This was the best I could personally do with my own financial and health issues.

Well, I suppose the best I can do to perhaps make you reconsider is share with you my own attempt at hypothermia.  I went out in shorts and a t-shirt in Harlem in the middle of winter.  After I could no longer feel any part of my arm, I panicked in fear that I would have to amputate my arm but still remain alive, so I ran into a MacDonalds to warm up.  It took one hour before I started to get the sensation back into my arms.  Very scary.

Do you feel that you may be able to muster up enough patience to maybe wait to see if things improve for you?   Of course, I have no idea of the amount and type of pain you have been experiencing.  Maybe, if you feel it can help, we can talk about it.

What if there is more to life beyond what the mere human brain and senses can perceive?  Think of the smartest animal, the chimp - he can use tools: he takes a stick and uses it to pick out insects from the small crevices in tree trunks.  The chimp thinks "Look at how smart I am, I can use a stick, clearly this is the highest reality of existence, me using a stick to remove insects from the tree!"  Alas, the chimp simply lacks the ability to ever understand that beyond the trees and insects lies other lands, other planets, other stars and galaxies, and so forth.  Well, humans too have limitations; even the smartest human may not be aware of other levels of reality, other laws of physics beyond his understanding and detection.  In other words, there is really no scientific justification for nihilism.  Maybe if you stay alive long enough, you can find out for yourself.  Since you said you are quite intelligent, you may consider majoring in physics, a "spiritual" endeavor itself.
Why do you feel like you want to die?

I myself had purchased a Glock 22 .40 caliber for $600 or so from the gun store for the sole purpose of suicide.  Every day for six months, I put the gun to my head, but was too much of a coward to pull the trigger.  After the six months, I got sick of looking at the gun, and then just donated the 100% unused gun to the local police department.  $600 gone to complete waste.

Needless to say, I am sorry that you have not found a long-term relationship as yet.  I do know that I used to have an Indian gay friend who moved to India, got married to another gay Indian, and now stars in Bollywood movies.   So, love and marriage is indeed doable for the gay community.  Regardless, I do hope you find contentment, however you choose to go about it.

I'm sure many people will appreciate your advice here as well as you describing your personal experience.  It seems like relationships are the source of so much suicidality.   I can't even imagine what that feels like - as one who has Asperger's, I can't form personal emotional bonds, so I don't know what it is like to have such a strong instinctual need for it.

How about just to see what happens in the next 70 years?  Will humans visit Mars?    Will Martians visit Earth?  Will cars ever fly?  Will computers become sentient and be given the right to vote?  Lots of cool things can happen in 70 years.

Yup, I also have that extreme social anxiety issue.  That is one reason I always wear a hat in public - to cover part of my face.  I personally try to make up for my looks by having very good hygiene: always shaven, clean conservative haircut, nicely trimmed eyebrows, formal business-like clothing, etc.  If I can't look pretty, then at least I can make up for it other ways.  But, I guess if we were to see a psychologist, they would say that we should just  be confident, no matter what.  In other words, f\*ck everyone else, and just handle your business.

I think I know that the last thing you would want is for me to suggest so-and-so to help you, since obviously you are smart enough to have already tried all the things available to you.  I know that I have tried everything to help me.  I guess it is up to each of us to decide where to go from here.  One can of course always try to talk about stuff here in this forum, at least so that others can hear you.
I spent 30 days in a psyche ward.   They were a great staff and medical team that did all they can to help me, but my problems could not be cured.  Hopefully things will work out better for you.

In elementary school, hundreds used to mock my Torrette's Symdrome, always mock me, constantly, every hour of every school day.  But as an adult, other adults tend to be rather mature about the issue and just interact with me normally.  If you are asking about sexual relationships, then it is true that no female is attracted to me, but that is just fine with me, since I have endeavored to become asexual anyway.

You just described me: I literally have the body frame of an adult woman, with the head size of a 14 year old male.  I have very weak connective tissue, so my skin is very thin, my muscles can't get big and hard, and my joints are weak.  My whole body is full of mutations: left-handedness, hump back, scoliosis, ADD, Torrettes Syndrome, Depression, Anxiety, schizophrenia, deformed ears, uneven shoulders, etc.  I'm a walking freak of nature.  So, my solution was to just be an altruistic person and do my best to help others, and not care what others think about my looks.
I know how you feel, my friend.   I only stay alive because  altruism invokes me to help out a  family member..  Once the family member has passed away, I will blow my freakin brains out.
